title: The two wills: the simple will in the Essence, and the general will that holds every detail in one glance
overview: Chapter 16 sets out to explain the circles of the *Kav*, "it circles, and goes back, and circles", but first the *Kav* in general, and it does so through the first circle, the *machshava kduma*, the *Malchus* of the line. There are two wills. The simple will is one with the Essence; the decided will inside it, the *glif glifu*, settles how everything will be, the way a man is born with a taste for a red car or a baroque house, and yet it is no separate decision, "as if it were not there". So *tehiru ila'a* is above *klal* and *prat*, and to call G-d "looking and seeing in one glance" is *avoda zara*. The second will, after the *tzimtzum*, is the *ratzon kadum*: "I want a car", which already holds the steering wheel, as the house holds the kitchen and the sink. It comes down as the will to emanate, the architect, the draftsman and the contractor, to the last nail. But what it wanted was only the end: the man at his *Shabbos* table with his wife, the schmaltz herring and the vodka.

sections.title: Before the details: the Kav as the hiyuli of everything, taught through its first circle
sections.summary: The chapter sets out to explain the circles of the *Kav*, but first the *Kav* in general: the *hiyuli* of everything down to the end of *Asiya*. He explains it through the first circle, the *machshava kduma*, which is the *Malchus* of the line, and which the *Rambam*'s "in knowing Himself He knows all the creatures" is really about.

phrases.he: (טז) והנה מעתה יש להבין בפרטי ענין הקו וחוט זה,
איך שיש בו בחינת מקיפים ופנימיים
כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים
מתעגל וחוזר ומתעגל כו'
phrases.en: it's *misagel*, and then it goes back, another line from that *igul* down, and then it's again *misagel*

phrases.he: (כמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות)
ובחינת מקיף ועיגול הראשון הוא הנקרא טהירו תתאה כו',
והוא בחינת המקיף הכללי שמקיף לד' עולמות דאבי''ע בשווה
כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים

blocks.text: Now the chapter turns to the particulars of the *Kav* and the thread: how there are encompassing lights and inner lights in it. In the words of the *Etz Chaim* it is *misagel v'chozer umisagel* (it circles, and goes back, and circles): it becomes an *igul* (a circle), then from that circle another line goes back down, and then it circles again. The first circle is the *tehiru tata'a*, the general *makif* of all four worlds of *ABYA* (*Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*), equally.

phrases.he: ותחלה יש להקדים כללות ענין הקו הזה,
phrases.en: but first let's understand what the general *inyan* of the *Kav* is

phrases.he: איך שהוא בחינת היולי כללי לכל הסתעפות המשכות פרטיים הרבה שמסתעפים ממנו עד סוף העשיה כו'
phrases.en: all kinds of things branch out all the way down to the end of *Asiya*; it is all from this line, it's the *hiyuli* for everything

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: But first we must preface the general matter of this *Kav*. That is what he is going to get into, but first one has to understand what the general *inyan* (matter) of the *Kav* is. All kinds of things branch out from it, all the way down to the end of *Asiya*, and it is all from this line: it is the *hiyuli* for everything.

phrases.he: ויובן זה על דרך משל הידוע בענין מחשבה כללית

blocks.text: He told you he is going to explain the line and how the line is a general *hiyuli*. But notice: he is not explaining the line, he is explaining the first circle, the *machshava kduma* (the primordial thought). In several places he calls the *machshava kduma* the line. That is because the *machshava kduma* is basically the end of the line: it is *Malchus* (kingship) of the line.

You may say the line is one thing and the *machshava kduma* another; it depends. The *kav katzar* (the short line) is in some places before even the *machshava kduma*, and it is still called *stima d'chol stimin* (the most hidden of all hidden), while the *machshava kduma* he will later call *Atika Stima'a* (the hidden Ancient One). And yet here, and in several other places, when he says the line he means the *machshava kduma*. The *Keser* (crown) of the *machshava kduma* comes out from *Malchus* of the line, so the *machshava kduma* is *mamash* the end of the *Malchus* of the line, the end of the end of the line. So it is still from the line. But that is the little line, the *kav hamida* (the line of measure) itself, and this is its *Malchus*: only ten points come out, and that's it.

phrases.he: שבמחשבה זו הכללית צופה ומביט עד סוף כל הדורות
בסקירה א'
(ובלשון הרמב''ם היינו מה שבידיעת עצמו יודע את כל הנבראים
כמו שכתוב במקום אחר)

blocks.text: He looks and sees to the end of all the generations, all of them, in one glance; in the *Rambam*'s language, in knowing Himself He knows all the creatures. So he is already telling us that what the *Rambam* said is not really talking about before the *tzimtzum* (contraction). It is a kabbalistic *inyan*: it is really talking about the *yichuda tata'a* (the lower unity).

In various places in the earlier books of Kabbala, when they talk about the *Atzmus* (the Essence), it is *Atik* and *Arich* (*Atik Yomin* and *Arich Anpin*, the levels of *Keser*) of *Atzilus* that they call the *Atzmus*. You have to know what they are talking about, because what he calls the *Atzmus* here is higher than *Yachid* (lit. singular, the first of the three levels). Remember we learned that higher than *Yachid* is the *Maor* (the source of light); the *Atzmus* is higher even than that. In most places *Atik* and *Arich* are called the *Atzmus*, and here too, when we get there, he will say it is still considered part of the *Atzmus*. And in some places it goes all the way to the outside, which is called the *gufa d'malka* (the body of the King): that is still the *Atzmus*, but it is the outside of the *Atzmus*. So even there you have to know what they are talking about.
Most people think that what the *Rambam* is saying, in knowing Himself He knows all the creatures, is the self, *mamash* the self. It's really not. It is the *machshava kduma*.

sections.title: The first will: the simple will in the Essence, with the decided will inside it
sections.summary: The simple will is one with the Essence; it is not even called a thought or a will. Within it is the decided will, the *glif glifu*, where it is already settled how each thing will be done; and still it is neither a *klal* nor a *prat*.

phrases.he: וביאור הדברים ידוע שיש ב' מיני רצון
א' רצון הפשוט שבעצמות שנכלל בעצמותו ממש,
שלא נקרא עדיין בשם בחינת מחשבה ורצון כללי
phrases.en: as a matter of fact, it's not even called a *machshava* and *ratzon* altogether

phrases.he: כי מתאחד עדיין בעצמותו ממש

blocks.text: there are two kinds of will. The first is the simple will in the Essence, included in His Essence *mamash*, which is not yet even called a thought or a general will. As a matter of fact, it is not even called a thought and a will at all. As was said in chapter 10, you have to say there is a thought and a will there only because you can't say that there isn't.

phrases.he: כמו גם שהוחלט רצון זה כבר בעצמו
phrases.en: He already decided exactly how it's going to be done

phrases.he: איך לעשות דבר חסד פלוני
או איך לדבר ולחשוב אותו
או להשכיל שכל פרטי
או להיות לו רצון ותענוג בדבר כו'

blocks.text: Now he is telling you that in the *ratzon hapashut* there are two levels, the *ratzon hapashut* and the *ratzon hamuchlat* (the decided will), and this is the second. The decided will is the *glif glifu* (He engraved an engraving). *Muchlat* means decided, from *hachlata* (a decision): He already decided exactly how it is going to be done, how to do such-and-such a kindness. It means the actual decision of the external.

In the *ratzon hamuchlat* too there are three levels, *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon* (singular, one and preceding). And it is the decision how to speak or think, or to conceive a particular idea, or to have a will and delight in a thing: so even when the actual decision is made, you have to say that the decision comes from the Essence itself.

phrases.he: הגם שמתחבר רצון המוחלט הזה אל התפשטות הרצון בדבר הפרטי
אבל נשאר כלול בהעלם עצמותו
phrases.en: it doesn't really come out, and does not actually have anything to do with the thing, even though the thing really comes out of it

phrases.he: ועל כן אין בו עדיין בחינת כלל ופרט כו'
phrases.en: there really is not a *klal*, not a *prat* there

blocks.text: The decided will connects to the spreading of the will into the particular thing, as was explained before, but it remains included in the hiddenness of His Essence. It doesn't really come out, and it really has nothing to do with the thing, even though the thing really comes out of it.

Therefore there is not yet in it a *klal* and a *prat*: there really is no *klal* (a general whole) there and no *prat* (a particular), even though from the other side you have to say that it has both, even the particulars. You can't say there is no *prat* there. Some people think this means that the Essence is a matter of a *klal*. But a real *klal* means that the particulars are not actually there yet, and of the Essence you can't say that.

sections.title: The composite will: "I want a car" holds every particular
sections.summary: Only when the decided will comes to an actual deed does it come out as *klal* and *prat*: one general thought, the *ratzon kadum*, a copy of the *glif glifu* through the *reshimu*, which holds the whole deed in one glance and then divides into particular wills, each encompassing the next like a wheel within a wheel. This is the composite will.

phrases.he: רק כאשר לאחר זה עולה רצון זה שהוחלט אצלו לבוא לידי מעשה בפועל ממש
phrases.en: when he decides to actually do it

phrases.he: הרי יוצא מהעלמו לגלוי
phrases.en: then it goes to revelation

phrases.he: אז יבוא הרצון בבחינת כלל ופרט,
phrases.en: then it comes in a way of a *klal* and *prat*

phrases.he: דהיינו מחשבה כללית שכוללת כל ענין המעשה מראש לסוף
phrases.en: meaning just, I want a car, and it includes everything

phrases.he: בסקירה א'

blocks.text: When He decides actually to do it, it goes out from its hiddenness to revelation. Then, at that point, the will comes in a way of *klal* and *prat*: a general thought that includes the whole deed from beginning to end in one glance. First of all it comes out as a *klal*.

This is so for any will that comes out to do a thing in actual fact. And remember that in relation to the Essence, this whole *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent), which by us looks like it's the whole thing, is by the *Aibershter* (the One Above) really like one little decision.

blocks.title: A man decides to buy a car
blocks.text: It's like a man who made a decision to buy a car. The will for a car was really already included in the simple will, even before the decision.

And the decided will did not really come out of the simple will in any way, because up there you can't really say there is a *ratzon hamuchlat* as against a *ratzon hapashut*, any more than you can say there are *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon*, or ten *sefiros* (the Divine attributes). You can't really say that. It is only that at one point the decision comes out, so the decision had to be there, and therefore we call it a *ratzon hamuchlat*. But it is not yet a *klal* for anything. Only when it comes out does it come as an actual *klal* and *prat*.

blocks.title: The red car
blocks.text: And when it comes out, there is one particular: to buy the car. This came out of the *ratzon hamuchlat*, and even the decision what kind of car he would like, what color, goes according to a predetermined taste he already had. He has a certain predilection for a red car. He was born like that.

By the *Aibershter* it is not quite like that: up there there is no real definition at all. In the soul there are actually ten *sefiros*, and each one comes in a particular way in each person. Some people have a little bit more of one and a little bit less of another, and that mix is their character. It is already in their soul. So the soul is not totally like up there, although in the soul too there are levels and levels and levels. But the basic thing is that the whole taste you call a *ratzon hamuchlat* is really just part of the *ratzon hapashut*. That's the way he is. It's not that he really had to go and make a decision.

That's the way he is, and that's why you say that at one point it came out as a decision, and the *ratzon kadum* (the preceding will) came out of it. The *ratzon kadum* for the car came out as a simple thought that includes everything: "I want a car."

The *machshava kduma* is basically a *tzimtzum* of the *glif glifu*. It is really the *reshimu* (the impression) that is a *tzimtzum* of the *glif glifu*, and that means the light went out of the letters: just the letters without the light. Someone who knows how to read the letters, the same as the *mashpia* (the giver), has the whole light in the letters anyway. Someone who doesn't know how to read the letters, it doesn't mean nothing to him. And this very *reshimu*, *mamash* the letters of the *glif glifu*, was copied over into the *machshava kduma*.

That is why it is called *Atika*: *atik* means a copy, as in *ha'atka* (copying). *Atik* has various meanings. One is a copy, one is old, and one is removed, as he is going to explain later from *ma'atik harim*, "he uproots mountains": he pulls them out and disconnects them. So it means disconnected, removed.

blocks.title: The printing press
blocks.text: The copy is not the original letters anymore. The *glif glifu* is like a *chosam hamis'hapech* (a reversing seal): there was a *glif glifu*, then the *glif glifu* turned over into the letters of the *reshimu*, and then the letters of the *reshimu* stamped the letters of the *machshava kduma*. You know how a printing press works: you have letters, they press down, and that's how you got this book. These letters are a whole different *metzius* (existence) of letters, but nonetheless they are the same letters as over there, an exact copy. So in the *ratzon kadum* there is an exact copy of what was there. What is it? The same *Ana Emloch* (I shall rule).

blocks.title: A home, by a man and by a squirrel
blocks.text: It comes in a general fashion, like "I want a car". The analogy actually used in Torah is "I want a house", a home actually: not a house but a home, a crib. The *Aibershter* wanted a *dira* (a dwelling) in the lower worlds, and a *dira* means a home. So what does a home mean? Well, it depends what you are. If you're a person, it means a house. If you're a squirrel, it means a hole in the tree; that's a home. It depends on what you are: that's how the home is going to be.

blocks.title: A car with a steering wheel?
blocks.text: When it comes out, it comes out as one thing, a car. The man just says, I decided to get a car. So you can ask him: "Are you going to get a car with a steering wheel?" "What do you mean? Of course! How can you get a car without a steering wheel?" "But when you thought, I'm going to get a car, did you think, I'm going to get a car with a steering wheel?" "No, I just thought I'm going to get a car." And it automatically included all the particulars: a steering wheel, seats, windows, engine, everything. That is the general thought that includes the whole deed from beginning to end in one glance: just "I want a car", and it includes everything.

phrases.he: ואחר כך מתחלק בו רצונות פרטיים
ולכל רצון שכל ומדות כו'
phrases.en: and each *ratzon* has its own *sechel* and *middos*

phrases.he: ובאין זה אחר זה בהשתלשלות
phrases.en: they come one after the other, with *hishtalshelus*

phrases.he: זה עליון מקיף לתחתון,
phrases.en: one is higher and *makif* on that one

phrases.he: כאשר יהיה האופן בתוך האופן כו'
phrases.en: like a wheel inside of a wheel

blocks.text: Afterwards it divides into particular wills: what kind of color he wants, what kind of shape, that it should have wheels, that it should have a good engine, and so on. And each will has its own *sechel* (intellect) and *middos* (emotions).

blocks.title: The house, the kitchen and the sink
blocks.text: the higher one encompassing the lower. A first, general explanation of this is a house, which is the basic analogy he gives. You go to the man and tell him, I want a house. "Oh, you want a house. So do you want a kitchen also?" "Well, of course I want a kitchen. I told you I want a house, so that means I want a kitchen." So inside the will for a house is a will for a kitchen. "Oh, you want a kitchen, so you want a sink?" "Well, of course I want a sink, 'cause I want a kitchen, that means I want a sink." "Oh, you want a sink? Good. So you want a sink to have a hole in the bottom?" "Of course! If you have a sink, you have to have a hole in the bottom."

So you see that each will includes inside of it more particular wills. The will for a house is a general will to the particular will of a kitchen, and the particular will of a kitchen is a general will to the various things in the kitchen, which again become general wills to the various things in them. That is a very physical analogy of how they come one after the other in *hishtalshelus*: one is higher and *makif* on the other, as the will for the house is *makif* on the will for the kitchen, as a wheel within a wheel.

phrases.he: והוא הנקרא רצון המורכב
phrases.en: it's called *ratzon hamurkav*

phrases.he: שיש בו כלל ופרט
phrases.en: it's made up of particulars

blocks.text: This is called the *ratzon hamurkav*, which has *klal* and *prat* in it. *Murkav* means composite: it is made up of particulars. The simple will is not made up of anything at all.

sections.title: The analogy of the man who builds a great house: a taste settled long before, then the plan from klal to prat
sections.summary: A man's taste in houses is in him before he ever decides to build: decided, yet not a separate decision, "as if it were not there". When he comes to build, it comes first as one general picture of the whole house, and then divides, will within will, down to the last detail.

phrases.he: ויובן זה על דרך משל הידוע,
אדם שרוצה לבנות בנין גדול
כפי הרצון שהוחלת מכבר אצלו להיות בו אופנים מיוחדים דוקא
phrases.en: it's already in his inner *hachlata* that it should be in a certain way

phrases.he: שאותו הרצון שהוחלט אצלו מכבר,
הגם שהוא בא במדה ותענוג מיוחד באופן כך וכך,
phrases.en: he has a particular taste, even before it came out to anything

phrases.he: וממילא בשכל ומדות בא בשיעור ומדה כו',
phrases.en: so since it's already in a certain way, *mimeila* it has to have, in *sechel* and *middos*, a *shiur* and *midda*, since the *shiur* and *midda* is the whole thing

phrases.he: אך כל זה הוא השיעור וההחלט שבעצמותו עדיין,
ונכלל בעצמו
והיה כלא היה כו'
phrases.en: it's like it doesn't really exist

blocks.text: a man who wants to build a great building: it is already in his inner decision that it should be in a certain way. He has a particular taste, even before it came out to anything. And since it is already a certain way, it has to come with a measure in intellect and emotions, since the measure is the whole thing. But all this is still the measure and decision within his own self: *hayah k'lo hayah* (as if it were not there), it doesn't really exist. It is just his personal taste, not an actual decision as a separate thing from what he is.

blocks.title: A modern house or the Addams Family house
blocks.text: In one person, the image of the house included inside him will be a very modern house, with everything square and stuff like that. Another, if he thinks of a house, thinks of the Addams Family house, with gargoyles and stuff like that. ("Baroque," a listener puts in. "A what?" "Baroque." "Baroque, yeah, that's it.") It is already so predisposed that if you know the person, you already know that if he would buy a house, he would buy this kind of a house.

But it doesn't mean he actually made an actual decision. That's not what the *ratzon hamuchlat* means: the *ratzon hamuchlat* is just part of the *ratzon hapashut*. It means that inside himself you have to say there is a point, because why was there a decision on the outside? Because it had to be on the inside. But on the inside it was not really a separate thing: it is as if it were not there; you can't really say that it is there at all.

phrases.he: רק כאשר לאחר זמן באה מחשבה זו לבא למעשה,
ניכר בו התחלקות אותן אופנים שונים ממש
שכבר הוחלט אצלו
בכל פרטיהם
phrases.en: and every particular little part

blocks.text: Only when, after some time, this thought comes to be acted on: this means the decision was already decided before he made the actual decision. He already had the predisposition for a certain house or a certain car ahead of time, even before the decision.

blocks.title: "She would love this dress"
blocks.text: Well, women go shopping. Somebody who knows another person very well says, "Oh, she would love this dress." "How do you know? She never saw this dress." "Well, because I know her. She would love this dress." So you mean that there is already a decision in her for this dress, even though she never saw the dress yet and might never see it. You can tell that she already has a will for this dress, a will and a delight. The will and delight are already decided, and it didn't come to action at all.

sensitivity.reason: Opens with a passing generalisation, "women go shopping".
sensitivity.publishable: Somebody who knows another person very well says, "Oh, she would love this dress." "How do you know? She never saw this dress." "Well, because I know her. She would love this dress." So you mean that there is already a decision in her for this dress, even though she never saw the dress yet and might never see it. You can tell that she already has a will for this dress, a will and a delight. The will and delight are already decided, and it didn't come to action at all.

blocks.text: Only when it comes to action, the division into those different features, *mamash*, is seen in it, exactly according to the decision, which he had already decided in all their particulars: every particular little part, what he would like, what kind of kitchen, what kind of bathroom. It all comes out, with all the particulars.

phrases.he: רק שמתחלה בא הרצון הזה בדרך כלל
phrases.en: it comes in a general way: just, I want a house

phrases.he: שיהיה לו בנין בציור כך וכך
phrases.en: it's for this particular house; it's like a baroque house or a modern house already

phrases.he: ואחר כך מתחלק בו רצון פרטי לכל ענין פרטי
phrases.en: and then, only afterwards (first he has to have the general *ratzon*), the general *ratzon* can divide into all the particular *pratim*

blocks.text: Except that first this will comes in a general way: just "I want a house". But even when he just says I want a house, it is a will for this particular house, of such-and-such a picture: it's a baroque house or a modern house already. And then, only afterwards, it divides into the particulars: first he has to have the general will, and then the general will can divide into all the particulars.

phrases.he: ויורד ובא בסדר והדרגה
phrases.en: it comes down *b'seder hadraga*

phrases.he: מכלל הראשון שכולל הכל בסקירה א'
phrases.en: from the first *klal*, that includes the whole house in one *skira*

phrases.he: לפרט רצון שהוא נקרא כלל לגבי רצונות המסתעפים ממנו
עד שבא אל רצון ושכל פרטי היותר אחרון שבסוף מעשה בכלות הכל כו'
phrases.en: till he comes to the final particular thing at the end of the *maaseh*

phrases.he: ודי למבין.
phrases.en: and this is enough to understand

blocks.text: It comes down in order and by steps from the first *klal*, which includes everything in one glance: the whole house. He just says I want a house, but in that "I want a house" he has an image in his brain of the whole entire house already, everything that he wants. When he says a house, it conjures up a whole image in his mind. It is all there in one glance: not one particular at a time, but the whole thing in one shot. From that it comes down to a particular will that is a *klal* to the wills that branch out from it, like the kitchen. The one glance of the first will divides into sub-wills, and each of those also comes in one glance: the whole kitchen, in one glance. And from it there is a spreading out of lower and lower wills, each in one glance.

until it comes to the very last particular will and intellect, at the end of the deed, the final particular thing; and this is enough for one who understands. "And now we're going to have to switch *meshalim*" (analogies): above, it is not really such a physical analogy as that.

sections.title: The nimshal above: tehiru ila'a is beyond even "one glance"
sections.summary: What He measured in Himself in *tehiru ila'a* is the decided will within the simple will: it never comes out of the Essence. So it is above *klal* and *prat*, and above even "looking and seeing in one glance"; to call G-d that is *avoda zara*.

phrases.he: והנמשל מכל זה יובן למעלה
בהפרש שבין בחינת טהירו עילאה ובין בחינת טהירו תתאה שלאחר הצמצום
דמה ששיער בעצמו בכח בטהירו עילאה כו'
הוא כמו ההחלט ברצון הפשוט שבעצמות הנזכר לעיל
שעדיין לא בא כלל לבחינת התפשטות חוץ מן העצמות עדיין
וגם שיתחבר מרצון המוחלט הזה אל התפשטות הרצון שאחר כך,
phrases.en: really it is connected, that's where it comes from

phrases.he: מכל מקום נשאר כלול בהעלם עצמות דאור אין סוף

blocks.text: The *nimshal* (what the analogy stands for) is understood above, in the difference between *tehiru ila'a* and *tehiru tata'a*. What He measured in Himself, in potential, in *tehiru ila'a* is like the decision in the simple will in the Essence, which has not yet come at all to spreading out outside the Essence. And though the spreading of the will afterwards really is connected to this decided will, and that's where it comes from, still it remains included in the hiddenness of the Essence of the *Ein Sof*.

phrases.he: ועל כן למעלה הוא מבחינת כלל
phrases.en: it's even higher than a *klal*

phrases.he: להיות נקרא צופה ומביט בסקירה א' כו'.
phrases.en: you can't say about it *tzofeh umabit b'skira achas*

blocks.text: Therefore it is above being a *klal*: it is even higher than a *klal*. You can't say it is a *klal*, you can't say it is a *prat*, and you can't even say that it is not a *klal* and a *prat*. And you can't say of it that it is "looking and seeing in one glance".

So some people think: "Oh, I know what G-d is. It's 'looking and seeing in one glance.'" That's *avoda zara* (idolatry), because he has told you that you can't say it is looking and seeing. It is higher still than looking and seeing in one glance; it is not even one glance. That's just the way He is. It's not looking at all.

sections.title: The second will, after the tzimtzum: the ratzon kadum, and what it really wanted
sections.summary: After the *tzimtzum* the decided will comes to spread out: that is the *Kav*, whose first *makif* is the *tehiru tata'a*, the will that includes all wills. It comes down as the will to emanate, the will to create, down to the last deed; but what it wanted was only the end, the way a man building a house wants only to sit at his *Shabbos* table with his wife.

phrases.he: אך הרצון הב' הוא אחר הצמצום הנזכר לעיל
שעולה רצון הפשוט המוחלט שבעצמות לבא לידי בחינת התפשטות
phrases.en: when it comes to spread out, that he actually is going to get a house

phrases.he: הוא בחינת הקו וחוט ההיולי
שכולל כל המשכות פרטיות שבו מראשו לסופו כנזכר לעיל
ובחינת מקיף הראשון שבו הוא הנקרא טהירו תתאה,
שזהו כמשל רצון הכללי לבנין גדול כולל כל מה שבפרטיו מראשו לסופו בבת א'
ואחר כך מתחלק בו בסדר והדרגה מכלל לפרט
על דרך משל הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: like we explained before

blocks.text: But the second will is after the *tzimtzum*, when the simple, decided will in the Essence arises to spread out: when it comes to spread out, that he actually is going to get a house. That is the all-including *hiyuli* power, which includes all the particular drawings-down from its beginning to its end. Its first *makif* is the *tehiru tata'a*, which is like the general will for a great building, including all its particulars from beginning to end at once; and afterwards it divides in order and by steps from *klal* to *prat*, as in the analogy explained before.

phrases.he: והיינו כמו כשעלה ברצונו הפשוט ההיולי לבא לגלוי דוקא,
היה כולל כל פרטי הרצונות
והוא הרצון הכולל כולם,
ונקרא רצון קדום לכל מה שבא אחריו
ואחר כך בא רצון זה דרך פרט,
phrases.en: this *ratzon klal*, the *ratzon kadum*, that's coming into the *pratim*

phrases.he: כמו הרצון להאציל
ובו כלול עשר ספירות בכל פרטיהם
ועדיין הכל בהעלם
phrases.en: this *prat*, the *ratzon l'ha'atzil*, is still *b'helem*

phrases.he: עד שבא לידי גלוי שהוא כשנאצל האור בבחינת האצילות כו'
phrases.en: it only comes in *gilui* when the actual *Atzilus* of the thing

blocks.text: When it arose in His simple, *hiyuli* will to come into revelation, it included all the particular wills. This is the will that includes them all, and it is called the *ratzon kadum* to all that comes after it. Afterwards this will comes in a particular way, like the will to emanate, in which the ten *sefiros* are included in all their particulars. (He corrects the reading: it does not say "and so on" but "in which are included": "It's a beis, not a kaf.")

and it is still all hidden. This general will, the *ratzon kadum*, coming into the particulars: this particular will, the will to emanate, is still hidden. It only comes into revelation with the actual *Atzilus* of the thing, when the four levels of *Atzilus* come about.

phrases.he: ואחר כך הרצון לברוא יש מאין כו'
ובו שכל ומדות כו'
עד הרצון היותר אחרון
שהוא כל אשר חפץ עשה כו',
סוף הכל
phrases.en: the end of everything

blocks.text: And then comes the will to create *yesh me'ayin*, with intellect and emotions in it, until the will for the last *Asiya*: "all that He desired, He did", which includes **the end of everything**, all the particular wills of the *Asiya*.

Now to take it back to the will for the house: what he is talking about here is not the same thing as the house and the kitchen. If you say a house and a kitchen and a sink, the main thing is not just the sink. Over here we are saying the main thing is the *Asiya*, and everything else, the *Atzilus* too, is just a *derech ma'avar* (a way of passing through). The real thing he wants is just the end thing.

So what does it mean? First comes the will to emanate. His will for the house was really part of the *ratzon hamuchlat*, and very simply, because it says that a person who doesn't have a house is not a person. And not only that: what he really wants is not a house, it's a home. As it says, *beiso zo ishto*: his house, that means his wife. He needs a place to live in with his wife. That's what he really wants.

The real thing he wants is a wife. Like we just learned with Lavan: the tent of Yaakov was the tent of Rachel. The verse called the others by their names, and this one it called the house of Yaakov. So his wife, that is the house. That's what he really wants.

blocks.title: The swimming pool that is a will to swim
blocks.text: Then comes the will to emanate. What is it? It is inside himself, because *Atzilus* is still not outside of himself. He has to look inside himself and know himself in relation to the house: what he wants from the house. So in the will to emanate, the swimming pool is not really a swimming pool: it's the delight and the will to swim. And the kitchen is not really a kitchen; it's the will to eat. He knows he likes to eat in a certain way, so he'll need a certain kitchen.

To come up with the house, the first thing he has to do is to be *ma'atzil* (to emanate), which means to be *mafrish* (to set apart) from his own personality what the *middos* of the house will be. The *middos* of the house are really his *middos*. If he's a *sechel* person, he'll have a *sechel* type of house. If he's a physical person, he'll want a tennis court or something like that. But really it's not a tennis court: it's his own desire to be a certain way. He has to clarify to himself what his wills are, and that's the *Atzilus* of the house.

blocks.title: The architect: Beriya
blocks.text: The next thing, he has to go to the level of *Beriya*, which means going to the architect. The architect has to take from *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, which becomes *Keser* of *Beriya*. What does it mean? The architect says to the man, "So what do you want from a house?" The only way he can make a perfect house for this man is to get from the *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, from what the man tells him, what he was *mesha'er* (measuring) inside himself, what he saw for himself in a house: his will and delight in a house. "What would you like? You want to make big parties? Do you want to entertain a lot, or you just want to sit by yourself and read books?" If he wants to sit by himself and read books, you have a den and a library. If he likes to entertain a lot, you're going to need a big kitchen and a large banquet room.

So the *Malchus* of *Atzilus* becomes *Keser* of *Beriya*. That is the will that gives the architect the whole thing he will want to design for this person, and it comes out in *dibur* (speech) to the architect: the *Malchus* of *Atzilus* is the *dibur*. The architect has to get out of him what he wants for a house, and when he tells him that, he is really telling him about himself, the *gufa d'malka*: his own body, who and what he is, what his desires are. If he's a guy that likes to have strong muscles, he'll want a weightlifting room. But in *Atzilus* it's not a weightlifting room yet: it's the *gufa d'malka*, the muscles of the king. The kitchen is his stomach. Each part of the house comes from a certain perception of himself, or even from a part of the body: the kitchen comes from the digestive tract, as does the bathroom.

blocks.question: The self-perception as a whole is Adam Kadmon; are we not talking about Atzilus already, and is the machshava kduma not Adam Kadmon?
blocks.text: No. We didn't get to the self-perception yet, and we are not talking about the actual *Atzilus*: this is all in the *machshava kduma*. He didn't go to the architect yet. Nor is the *machshava kduma* *Adam Kadmon* (primordial man, the first world): it is the *Keser* of whatever it is, before *Adam Kadmon*. Over here there is not even a will for *Atzilus* yet. The *Atzilus* is just automatically included: when he has the *machshava kduma* for the house, it includes the *Atzilus* of a house within itself, within himself. So we are not talking about the actual *Atzilus* yet; we are talking about the *machshava kduma*, whatever that is. It is the *Atzilus* as it is included in the *machshava kduma*, the *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*.

And what is *Yetzira*? He starts to say *Yetzira* is when the architect came out with a concept of the house, and then puts it right: that is still *Beriya*. It is no longer the concept of the person. It's a *Beriya*, a new creation, something from nothing. Before, it wasn't a house, it was a person. Now it's the concept of a house, a new creation, something from nothing, which the architect created according to the shape of a person, and then it is taken to the contractor.

blocks.title: The perfect chair
blocks.text: Or, for instance, a chair. The actual *etzem* of the chair is a *tachas* (a behind). That's the man himself. If you want to create the perfect chair, you have to know what a behind is like, and also what a back is, and the arms: the whole thing. You have to know the person, the measurements. ("Like the *shiur koma* (the full stature)," a listener says. "The *shiur koma*, that's what we were talking about in *Adam Kadmon*. But this is before still. It's just a *machshava kduma*.")

And that's the *Yetzira*. In *Beriya* the concept is still just a concept. *Yetzira* is when the architect gives the concept over to the draftsman, the guy who draws the form. It's still not *mamash* a house, but *Yetzira* means you make the form: you fashion the form of the thing, and that is the drafting of the entire plan that was created in *Beriya* something from nothing. Now it's turned into an actual form.

And then *Asiya* is when you go to the contractor. The *Keser* of *Yetzira* comes from *Malchus* of *Beriya*: the architect tells the draftsman what he came up with. Then the draftsman comes up with an actual blueprint, and the final blueprint is like *Malchus* of *Yetzira*, which tells the contractor the final form, and that becomes the *Keser* of *Asiya*: now he wants to make a house according to the blueprint. This goes all the way down to the last nail in the house, which is included in the *machshava kduma*.

When the contractor finishes the house, then there's the house itself. And when the man moves into the house, furnishes it and moves in with his wife, that's the *machshava kduma* itself. That was really it: the real desire, the real original design. You see, this is not really even *Asiya*. It's really the product of *Asiya*.

blocks.title: "Here's your money, get out of here"
blocks.text: It's not the contractor; now we don't need a contractor no more. The contractor stays there, and the man says: "What are you doing here? You finished building the house, here's your money, get out of here. What do I need you for? Get out of my house. Get out of here. My wife is coming any minute, I don't want her to see these guys." So the actual final product is in a way not really a part of the *hishtalshelus*, and yet it is the real *machshava kduma*.

blocks.title: Schmaltz herring and vodka on Shabbos
blocks.text: As a matter of fact, the real *machshava kduma* was not even for the house. It was *Shabbos*, when he sits there with his guests, and his wife lit the candles, and they have a nice bottle of wine on the table, and they bring out the schmaltz herring and the vodka. That's what was in the *machshava kduma*.

The *machshava kduma* included the whole process of getting there, but in the *machshava kduma* itself he really didn't think of the process. He did not think at all of *Atzilus* all the way down to *Asiya*. He just thought directly of the last thing: I want a home, my wife. The home is the wife: the home is the fact that he sits there with his wife, not the fact that there are walls. That's why by a squirrel a home doesn't mean walls, it just means where he sits with his wife: a hole in a tree, or by a bird, a nest. So the main thing is the wife. The home is the place where the family is: him with his family, a place for him to live, a *dira*. All this is the end of the deed, **the end of everything**.

phrases.he: וכל פרטים הללו נכללו ברצון הקדום
phrases.en: they're already included in the *ratzon kadum*

phrases.he: שבא בבחינת השפעה על כל פנים אחר הצמצום

blocks.text: All these particulars were included in the *ratzon kadum*, which comes as *hashpa'a* (giving forth), at least after the *tzimtzum*. In the *ratzon kadum* you could sort of say it is already in the way of *hashpa'a*, but really it is not *hashpa'a*. The *ratzon kadum* is really still for himself. It's not even for the house, it's for the home: for the delight he is going to get, really for his own delight.

sections.title: The beginning of the Kav and the first circle: circle within circle, down to a slice of pizza
sections.summary: The *ratzon kadum* is called both the beginning of the *Kav* and the circle after it, because its *Keser* comes from the *Malchus* of the beginning of the *Kav*. From each circle a line goes down to the next circle, which is again a *ratzon kadum* to what is inside it: that is "it circles, and goes back and circles".

phrases.he: והוא בחינת ראשית הקו כו',
phrases.en: and that is the beginning of the line

phrases.he: והיינו עיגול הראשון שאחר המשכת ראשית הקו ההיולי הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: that is the *igul harishon* (the first circle), which is after the *reishis hakav*

phrases.he: שנקרא מקיף כללי לכללות כל הד' עולמות דאבי''ע, שמקיף אותם בשוה
שנקרא מחשבה כללית שצופה ומביט בסקירה א' מראש לסוף הכל כו'

blocks.text: And it is the *reishis hakav*, the beginning of the line: that is, the first circle, after the drawing-down of the beginning of the line. So what is he saying here? He said two opposite things. He says that's the *reishis hakav*, and that it is the first circle, which is after the *reishis hakav*. So again, it depends which *Kav* you are talking about. There is the *hiyuli* line, the first *hiyuli* line, and then there is the next *Kav*, which will include everything to the end of *Adam Kadmon*; that is the beginning of *Adam Kadmon*. And this is called the general *makif* of all four worlds of *ABYA*, encompassing them equally, the general thought that looks and sees in one glance from beginning to end.

phrases.he: וזהו ביאור ענין כללי לכללות ענין הקו הזה

blocks.text: You notice he says this is the explanation of the general matter of this *Kav*, and yet he didn't talk about the *Kav* at all in this whole chapter. He talked about the *machshava kduma*, and he is calling it the *Kav*. And he also said: the first circle, after the *reishis hakav*. Before that he said: they were included in the *ratzon kadum*, which comes as *hashpa'a* at least after the *tzimtzum*, "and it is the *reishis hakav*". So he is calling the *ratzon kadum* the *reishis hakav*, and then he says it is after the *reishis hakav*. In the same sentence! ("In the same sentence," a listener echoes.)

So basically the explanation is that the *ratzon kadum* is after the *reishis hakav*, but the *Keser* of the *ratzon kadum* comes from *Malchus* of the *reishis hakav*: of the ten points, the end point is the point of *Malchus* of the *reishis hakav*. And really it is not considered the actual *reishis hakav*. It is *Malchus* of *Malchus* of the *reishis hakav*, and not even really *Malchus* of *Malchus*, but how *Malchus* of *Malchus* comes to become the *Keser* of the next rung, the next thing down. And this *reishis hakav* that the *machshava kduma* is, the *Kav* that comes down from the *machshava kduma*, includes all the worlds: it is a general *makif*.

phrases.he: ופרטי אופניו במה שמתעגל וחוזר ומתעגל כו'
יובן לפי אופן משל הנזכר לעיל
וכמו שיתבאר בסמוך בעזרת ה׳ ודי למבין:

blocks.text: in that it circles, and goes back and circles: the circling he did describe. The going back and circling he never said anywhere; but really he did, when he spoke of the four worlds, and he is going to explain the matter of the circles. The basic thing is that the *reishis hakav* comes to the first circle, and he explained how that happens: from the *tzimtzum*, from the *reshimu*, to the beginning, to the *machshava kduma*. Then from the *machshava kduma*, which has the quality of a circle, comes a line to the next particular, which is again a circle: the general will, again, for what is inside it. He actually did tell us: a wheel inside a wheel. In general he explained it, and it works the same way: when the lower circle comes, it again is like a *machshava kduma* to what is inside it.

blocks.title: A piece of pizza
blocks.text: As a matter of fact, each will is like that, all the way down to even a will for a pizza. A guy has a will for pizza: "Oh, hey, I'd like a piece of pizza." That already includes all the wills in it: to go look for his wallet, to get his car key, to drive in the car, to go to the pizza place, to joke with the guy at the pizza place, everything. But what he really wanted is the end of the whole thing: he's going to get the pizza. That's what he actually wanted. In the *ratzon kadum* it was a will for a pizza.

And so even when it comes from a general will to a particular will, that particular will again becomes like a *ratzon kadum* to everything inside it, and it comes in one glance of everything. So really he did explain it: that is it circles, and goes back and circles, and it will be understood according to the analogy and what it stands for, as will be explained shortly, with G-d's help.

reviewQuestions.question: Why does he say the chapter, which promises to explain the *Kav*, is really explaining the *machshava kduma*, and how can that still be called the line?
What is the *Rambam*'s "in knowing Himself He knows all the creatures" really talking about, and why does it matter what the books of Kabbala call the *Atzmus*?
How can there be a decided will inside the simple will, when there is no *klal* and no *prat* in it? Use the man with the predilection for a red car.
What does the steering wheel show about the general thought, and what does the house, the kitchen and the sink add to it?
Why is it *avoda zara* to say that G-d is "looking and seeing in one glance"?
In the house analogy of the four worlds, what are *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, and what was the *machshava kduma* really for?

notes.text: Class 014 reads line 13 twice: once straight after line 12 (w1525-1555), then again at w2699 after the long explanation. Lines 12 and 13 are one passage, so the whole explanation sits under both.
He cites "a person who doesn't have a house is not a person" with "it says" and no source; left as he said it. The reviewer may want to check the wording of the saying he has in mind.
On Lavan's search he first says "the tent of Leah", then corrects himself to Rachel; the block gives the corrected version. (Rashi on Genesis 31:33 says Yaakov's tent was Rachel's.)

Class 024 w1110-1259 is a back-and-forth with no speaker labels; the split between the student's question (self-perception as Adam Kadmon, "Atzilus already", "so the machshava kduma is Adam Kadmon") and his answers is my reading. He says the machshava kduma is "before Adam Kadmon" and also "Keser of Adam Kadmon"; both are kept.
Class 024 w1260-1303: he begins "what is Yetzira? when the architect came out with a concept", then calls that a Beriya; Yetzira proper comes at w1446. The block says he puts it right.
Class 014 line 30: he reads "the general hiyuli power" where the text has "the Kav v'chut, the hiyuli"; the phrase follows the text, the block what he said.
Class 024 line 36: the reading is corrected from "and so on" to "in which are included" ("It's a beis, not a kaf"); it is not clear whether he or the reader first misread.

Several listener interjections ("Baroque", "the dibur", "like the shiur koma", "my wife", "in the same sentence") have no speaker label; they are given as a listener's where the next sentence answers them, otherwise folded into his words.

The aside at 014 w4141-4203 ("That's avoda zara") is not flagged: it is said of a theological idea (that G-d is "looking and seeing in one glance"), not of people or of a practice, and a public edition of a Chassidus class can print it as it stands.

terms is trimmed to 12 key terms; the incidental words (mafrish, mesha'er, ma'atzil, tachas, beiso zo ishto, ha'atka, ma'atik harim, derech ma'avar, hachlata, shiur koma and others) are glossed inline at first use only. None of them is in translit.json, except ma'atzil, added when the chapters were merged.
